content: Doxycycline monohydrate capsules should be used exclusively for the treatment or prevention of infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria susceptible to this antibiotic. This approach is essential to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the effectiveness of doxycycline and other antibacterial agents. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological and susceptibility patterns may inform empirical therapy decisions. Doxycycline is indicated for the treatment of the following infections: 1. Rickettsial infections: This includes Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus fever and the typhus group, Q fever, rickettsialpox, and tick fevers caused by Rickettsiae. 2. Respiratory tract infections: Caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae. 3. Lymphogranuloma venereum: Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. 4. Psittacosis (ornithosis): Caused by Chlamydia psittaci. 5. Trachoma: Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. However, the infectious agent may not always be eradicated, as determined by immunofluorescence testing. 6. Inclusion conjunctivitis: Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. 7. Uncomplicated infections of the urethra, endocervix, or rectum in adults: Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. 8. Nongonococcal urethritis: Caused by Ureaplasma urealyticum. 9. Relapsing fever: Due to Borrelia recurrentis. Doxycycline is also indicated for infections caused by the following gram-negative microorganisms: 1. Chancroid: Caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. 2. Plague: Due to Yersinia pestis (formerly Pasteurella pestis). 3. Tularemia: Due to Francisella tularensis (formerly Pasteurella tularensis). 4. Cholera: Caused by Vibrio cholerae (formerly Vibrio comma). 5. Campylobacter fetus infections: Caused by Campylobacter fetus (formerly Vibrio fetus). 6. Brucellosis: Due to Brucella species, in conjunction with streptomycin. 7. Bartonellosis: Due to Bartonella bacilliformis. 8. Granuloma inguinale: Caused by Calymmatobacterium granulomatis. Because many strains of certain microorganisms have demonstrated resistance to doxycycline, culture and susceptibility testing are recommended. Doxycycline is indicated for infections caused by the following gram-negative microorganisms when bacteriologic testing confirms susceptibility to the drug: 1. Escherichia coli 2. Enterobacter aerogenes (formerly Aerobacter aerogenes) 3. Shigella species 4. Acinetobacter species (formerly Mima species and Herellea species) 5. Respiratory tract infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae 6. Respiratory and urinary tract infections caused by Klebsiella species Doxycycline is also indicated for infections caused by the following gram-positive microorganisms when bacteriologic testing confirms susceptibility: 1. Upper respiratory infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (formerly Diplococcus pneumoniae). 2. Skin and skin structure infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus. 3. Anthrax due to Bacillus anthracis, including inhalational anthrax (post-exposure), to reduce the incidence or progression of disease following exposure to aerosolized Bacillus anthracis. Doxycycline is not the drug of choice for treating staphylococcal infections of any type. However, when penicillin is contraindicated, doxycycline serves as an alternative treatment for the following infections: 1. Uncomplicated gonorrhea caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. 2. Syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum. 3. Yaws caused by Treponema pertenue. 4. Listeriosis due to Listeria monocytogenes. 5. Vincent’s infection caused by Fusobacterium fusiforme. 6. Actinomycosis caused by Actinomyces israelii. 7. Infections caused by Clostridium species. In cases of acute intestinal amebiasis, doxycycline may be a useful adjunct to amebicides. Additionally, in severe acne, doxycycline may serve as a beneficial adjunctive therapy.
